description:
FILED s431 (Opus 5), found while probing #458.

    sub sh { print "n=", scalar(@_), " [", join("][", @_), "]\n" }
    $_ = 'aaaccc';
    sh(/a*b/, "d");     # perl: n=1 [d]      PCL: n=2 [][d]
    sh(/a/,   "d");     # perl: n=2 [1][d]   PCL: n=2 [1][d]   (right)
    my @l = (/zzz/);    # perl: 0            PCL: 0            (right)

perlop: "in list context a failed match returns the empty list".  The ASSIGNMENT path is right; the ARGUMENT-LIST path is not -- a failed match yields a false SCALAR that then flattens as one element.  So the divergence is in the arg-list flattening of a match's list value, not in the match itself.

WHY IT MATTERS: any `foo(/re/, ...)` with a failing match silently shifts every later argument by one -- the classic silent-wrong shape (CLAUDE.md 12 family).

BAR: the three probes above + a captured-group form (`sh(/(a)(b)/, "d")` on a failing match), grep/map/sort argument positions, and a `wantarray`-visible sub; corpus-diff; a Pl/t guard row of the oracle form.

=== CLOSED s463au (agent AU, round 20) â THIS IS #962, filed twice.  The fix
=== is in #962's SHIPPED section; the record is not duplicated here.

One correction to this task's own diagnosis, because it pointed at the wrong
layer: it says "the divergence is in the arg-list flattening of a match's list
value, not in the match itself".  It is in the MATCH.  do-regex-match returned
raw NIL in list context, and raw nil is the runtime's empty list to ONE
consumer only (%p-flatten-list); p-flatten-args spreads it as one argument and
p-array-fill keeps it as an array hole.  The ASSIGNMENT path looked right only
because `my @l = (/zzz/)` has nothing after the nil for the phantom slot to
shift.  `my @l = (/zzz/, "b")` was 2 in PCL and 1 in perl, and so was the
capture-bearing `(/(z)(z)/, "b")` â the arm is shared.

Fixed by returning `(%p-empty-list)` (a zero-length vector, the shape the
success arm and the /g list arm already yield), so every consumer splices it
to nothing without an arm of its own.  Bars in #962.  Guard rows include this
task's own three probes verbatim (`Pl/t/match-vars-01.t` row 35).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a FAILED match in list context inside an argument list contributes one EMPTY STRING instead of the empty list -- `f(/nomatch/, "d")` gets 2 args where perl gets 1
